name: Kentigern
text: Kentigern, or St Kentigern, who died in about ad 612, is remembered as the first bishop of Glasgow and ranks among the leading saints of the north of Britain. The name, drawn from Celtic *Kuno-tegernos, means 'hound lord', though people usually called him Mungo. Two twelfth-century vitae preserve the oldest reaches of his tale. Bishop Herbert (1147–64) sponsored an early fragmentary life, and Jocelin of Furness wrote a fuller version under Bishop Jocelin (1175–99); both rest on early medieval material whose reliability is hard to judge. Tradition says he was a grandson of the king who ruled Lothian, learned from St Serf at Culross, and took up the monastic life. He then travelled to Glasgow to lay to rest a holy man, Fergus, in a standing cemetery, and he lived in the Annandale district at Hoddom and also at Glasgow. Eight dedications in the present county of Cumbria mark his long-standing cult.
